content_voiceover: This slide moves into the molecularly informed myelofibrosis risk models, MIPSS70, MIPSS70 plus version 2, and GIPSS, plus a separate model for secondary myelofibrosis. MIPSS70 combines clinical variables, anemia, leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, blasts, constitutional symptoms, and bone marrow fibrosis, with the molecular finding of absence of a good risk CALR type one mutation, plus high risk mutations in ASXL1 and SRSF2. MIPSS70 plus version two refines this further, dropping leukocytosis, thrombocytopenia, and marrow fibrosis as standalone variables, but adding high risk karyotype and expanding the mutation panel to include EZH2 and IDH1 or IDH2 mutations alongside ASXL1 and SRSF2. GIPSS, the genetically inspired score, is purely genetic, no clinical variables at all, using only high risk karyotype, absence of good risk CALR type one, and high risk ASXL1 or SRSF2 mutations, plus U2AF1 mutation which appears only in GIPSS and MIPSS70 plus, not in the original MIPSS70. On the right, a completely separate tool, the MYSEC-PM, or myelofibrosis secondary to PV and ET prognostic model, designed specifically for secondary myelofibrosis rather than primary myelofibrosis. It incorporates age at secondary MF diagnosis, hemoglobin under eleven, platelet count under one hundred fifty thousand, circulating blasts three percent or more, CALR unmutated genotype, and constitutional symptoms. Fellows should recognize that secondary myelofibrosis arising from PV or ET needs this dedicated model rather than the primary myelofibrosis scores.
keypoints: MIPSS70 combines clinical variables with CALR, ASXL1, and SRSF2 mutation status
MIPSS70 plus V2.0 adds karyotype and expands mutations to include EZH2, IDH1, IDH2, and U2AF1
GIPSS is purely molecular and cytogenetic, with no clinical variables at all
Absence of good risk CALR type one mutation is a shared high risk feature across all three scores
MYSEC-PM is a separate model specifically for myelofibrosis secondary to PV or ET
keypoint_voiceover: The molecular progression to remember is MIPSS70 blends clinical and mutation data, MIPSS70 plus version two adds karyotype and more mutations, and GIPSS is entirely genetic with no clinical input. Absence of a good risk CALR type one mutation is the common thread across all three. And remember, secondary myelofibrosis from PV or ET gets its own dedicated tool, the MYSEC-PM, not the primary myelofibrosis scores.
